items.followUp: Describe lactic acid fermentation and state where it occurs.

rubric.why: Identifies the organism and oxygen conditions for alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.description: Occurs in yeast when oxygen is absent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for yeast and anaerobic conditions (or equivalent).

rubric.why: Gives the characteristic products of alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.description: Glucose is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both products; the balanced equation is also acceptable.

modelAnswer: Alcoholic fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose by yeast.
Glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide + energy. (C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ + energy)

items.followUp: What is the role of oxygen at the end of the electron transport chain?

rubric.why: Identifies the electron transport chain and its location.
rubric.description: The electron transport chain is a series of electron carriers in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a carrier chain and its mitochondrial location.

rubric.why: Explains electron transfer and its connection to ATP formation.
rubric.description: Electrons pass along the carriers to oxygen; the released energy is used to make ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for electron transfer to oxygen and/or the resulting energy being used to form ATP.

modelAnswer: The electron transport chain is a series of electron carriers in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Electrons pass from one carrier to another and finally to oxygen; the released energy is used to produce ATP.

items.followUp: What is meant by organ transplantation?

rubric.why: Identifies vascular surgery as a surgical field concerned with blood vessels.
rubric.description: Vascular surgery is surgery involving blood vessels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking surgery with blood vessels.

rubric.why: States the conditions or vessels treated in this field.
rubric.description: It treats diseases or disorders of arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning treatment of blood-vessel disorders or naming arteries and veins.

modelAnswer: Vascular surgery is the branch of surgery concerned with blood vessels.
It treats diseases and disorders of arteries and veins.

items.followUp: Explain any four branches of Biology as careers.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant role for a career in medicine.
rubric.description: Medicine involves diagnosing, preventing and treating diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of medicine as a career.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant role for a career in agriculture.
rubric.description: Agriculture applies biology to improve crops and food production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of agriculture as a career.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant role for a career in animal husbandry.
rubric.description: Animal husbandry involves breeding and rearing useful animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of animal husbandry as a career.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant role for a career in fisheries.
rubric.description: Fisheries concerns fish breeding, rearing and production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of fisheries as a career.

modelAnswer: Medicine applies Biology to diagnose, prevent and treat diseases in humans.
Agriculture applies Biology to improve crops and increase food production.
Animal husbandry involves breeding and rearing animals for useful products.
Fisheries involves breeding, rearing and producing fish.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of the cell wall.

rubric.why: States the membrane’s key role in regulating exchange with the surroundings.
rubric.description: The cell membrane forms the cell boundary and selectively controls substances entering and leaving the cell.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for describing the boundary and controlled movement of materials.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic bilayer structure of the membrane.
rubric.description: The membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the phospholipid bilayer.

rubric.why: Identifies proteins positioned within or on the lipid bilayer.
rubric.description: Proteins are embedded in or associated with the bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for membrane proteins and their position.

rubric.why: Explains why the membrane is described as a fluid mosaic.
rubric.description: Lipids and proteins can move within the membrane, giving it a flexible, mosaic appearance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the model to mobile components and the membrane’s mosaic structure.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane forms the boundary of the cell and protects its contents.
It is selectively permeable, controlling the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
According to the fluid mosaic model, the membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer.
Protein molecules are embedded in or associated with the bilayer.
The lipids and proteins can move within the membrane, making it flexible and mosaic in appearance.

items.followUp: Explain how pH affects the rate of enzyme action.

rubric.why: Defines an enzyme by its catalytic role.
rubric.description: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up chemical reactions in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining an enzyme as a biological catalyst.

rubric.why: Explains the initial increase in enzyme activity as temperature rises.
rubric.description: As temperature rises, molecules gain kinetic energy and collide more often, so the reaction rate increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the temperature-related increase in reaction rate or its cause.

rubric.why: Identifies the temperature at which enzyme activity is highest.
rubric.description: The rate rises to an optimum temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the optimum temperature or peak activity.

rubric.why: Explains why high temperature reduces enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Above the optimum, the enzyme may denature and its active site changes, so the rate falls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for denaturation or loss of active-site shape causing a reduced rate.

modelAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up chemical reactions in living organisms.
As temperature rises, enzyme and substrate molecules gain kinetic energy and collide more frequently, so the reaction rate increases.
The rate reaches its maximum at the enzyme’s optimum temperature.
Above the optimum, the enzyme may denature and its active site changes shape, causing the rate to decrease.

items.followUp: Compare aerobic respiration with lactic acid fermentation.

rubric.why: Defines aerobic respiration by its use of oxygen and complete breakdown of glucose.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration is the complete breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both oxygen and complete breakdown.

rubric.why: Defines anaerobic respiration by its oxygen-free, incomplete breakdown of glucose.
rubric.description: Anaerobic respiration is the incomplete breakdown of glucose without oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both absence of oxygen and incomplete breakdown.

rubric.why: Names the two main types of anaerobic respiration covered here.
rubric.description: The two types are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types.

rubric.why: Describes the products of alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.description: In yeast, alcoholic fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying yeast and both products, or the two products with the process named.

rubric.why: Describes lactic acid fermentation and its product or site.
rubric.description: Lactic acid fermentation produces lactic acid, for example in muscle cells or certain bacteria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming lactic acid and a valid site or process.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the complete breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen, releasing energy.
Anaerobic respiration is the incomplete breakdown of glucose without oxygen and releases less energy.
The two types of anaerobic respiration are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.
In alcoholic fermentation, yeast converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.
In lactic acid fermentation, glucose is converted into lactic acid, as in muscle cells or certain bacteria.

items.followUp: Explain how mineral ions are absorbed by root hairs and transported through a plant.

rubric.why: Connects root-hair structure with effective absorption from the soil.
rubric.description: Root hairs are extensions of epidermal cells; their large surface area and thin walls aid uptake.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for root hairs and how their structure increases absorption.

rubric.why: Identifies osmosis as the route by which water enters root hairs.
rubric.description: Water enters root hairs from the soil by osmosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming osmosis for water uptake.

rubric.why: Distinguishes ion uptake from water uptake and identifies its mechanism.
rubric.description: Mineral ions are absorbed by active transport, using energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for active transport of mineral ions (energy or ATP may be mentioned).

rubric.why: Describes the route of absorbed water and ions into the conducting tissue.
rubric.description: Water and ions move through the cortex and endodermis into the xylem for transport through the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for tracing movement through root tissues into the xylem.

modelAnswer: Root hairs are extensions of epidermal cells; their large surface area and thin walls help absorb water and mineral ions from the soil.
Water enters root hairs by osmosis because water moves from the soil into the root-hair cells.
Mineral ions enter root hairs mainly by active transport, which requires energy.
Water and ions pass through the cortex and endodermis into the xylem.
The xylem carries them from the root to the rest of the plant.
